official_title.value: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Operationally Seamless, Adaptive Phase 2/3 Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Baricitinib in Adult Patients With Severe or Very Severe Alopecia Areata

mechanism_of_action.source_excerpt: openFDA drug/label mechanism_of_action (FDA-approved label, section 12.1) -- extracted text: 12.1 Mechanism of Action Baricitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor. JAKs are intracellular enzymes which transmit signals arising from cytokine or growth factor-receptor interactions on the cellular membrane to influence cellular processes of hematopoiesis and immune cell function. Within the signaling pathway, JAKs phosphorylate and activate Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription (STATs) which modulate intracellular activity including gene expression. Baricitinib modulates the signaling pathway at the point of JAKs, preventing the phosphorylation and activation of STATs. JAK enzymes transmit cytokine signaling through their pairing (e.g., JAK1/JAK2, JAK1/JAK3, JAK1/TYK2, JAK2/JAK2, JAK2/TYK2). In cell-free isolated enzyme assays, baricitinib had greater inhibitory potency at JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 relative to JAK3. In human leukocytes, baricitinib inhibited cytokine induced STAT phosphorylation mediated by JAK1/JAK2, JAK1/JAK3, JAK1/TYK2, or JAK2/TYK2 with comparable potencies. However, the relevance of inhibition of specific JAK enzymes to therapeutic effectiveness is not currently known.

topical calcineurin inhibitors (except on scalp, eyebrows, eyelids)
up to 2 intra-articular/soft-tissue corticosteroid injections before Week 36 (unlimited after)
bimatoprost ophthalmic solution (stable dose >=8 weeks prior to randomization)
finasteride/5-alpha reductase inhibitors or oral/topical minoxidil (stable dose >=12 months prior to randomization)
concomitant therapies for unrelated medical conditions (e.g. diabetes, hypertension)
value.population_note: Baricitinib is dosed as monotherapy for AA (regimen_type=monotherapy fits: Section 7.7.2 states any other investigational/commercial AA therapy or phototherapy is prohibited). Permitted concomitant medications listed are for unrelated conditions or for scalp/eyebrow/eyelid-excluded topical use, not a study-mandated background regimen for AA itself.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 7.7.2 Prohibited Medications and Procedures: "Any investigational or commercial topical, intra-lesional or systemic therapies (except those listed in Section 7.7.1) or phototherapy to treat AA are not allowed during the trial." Section 7.7.1 Permitted Medications and Procedures lists: "Topical corticosteroids except on the scalp, eyebrows, and eyelids... Topical calcineurin inhibitors except on the scalp, eyebrows and eyelids... A maximum of 2 intra-articular or soft tissue... corticosteroid injections are allowed up until the 36-week primary endpoint... Bimatoprost ophthalmic solution... Finasteride... or oral or topical minoxidil... HMG CoA reductase inhibitors."

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: SAP Section 4.6 Multiple Comparisons/Multiplicity: "Multiplicity adjusted analyses will be performed on the primary and key secondary objectives using the FAS population in order to control the overall familywise Type I error rate at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.05. The graphical multiple testing procedure described in Bretz et al. (2011) will be used. The graphical approach is a closed testing procedure; hence, it strongly controls the familywise error rate across all endpoints (Alosh et al. 2014)... The primary endpoint for both doses will be first tested at a two-sided a=0.025... Each time a hypothesis is rejected, the graph is updated to reflect the reallocation of a, which is considered 'recycled'."

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Section 5.1 Study Design: "The study design includes 5 periods: a 5-week screening period, a 36-week double-blind, placebo-controlled treatment period, a 68-week long-term extension period, a 96-week bridging extension, and a posttreatment follow-up period." Section 5.1.5: "The primary efficacy endpoint will be at Week 36 (Visit 8)." Section 5.1.7: "Patients who have completed Week 104... will have the possibility to remain in the trial for up to 96 additional weeks (up to Week 200)."

value.rationale: BRAVE-AA1 is a response-adaptive dose-rescue design rather than an escape-medication design: nonresponders are 'rescued' by moving from placebo, or from a lower baricitinib dose, onto (or up to) baricitinib 4-mg -- not switched to a different rescue drug class. No topical/systemic escape medication outside the study drug itself is offered; all other AA therapies remain prohibited throughout (Section 7.7.2).

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 5.1.6, Period 3: Long-Term Extension, 'At Week 36': "Patients in the placebo treatment arm who have not achieved SALT <=20 at Week 36... will be rescued to baricitinib and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to baricitinib 2-mg or baricitinib 4-mg." 'At Week 52', Nonresponders: "Those who have been in the baricitinib 2-mg treatment group from Baseline will be rescued to baricitinib 4-mg." And under Responders: "Responders who experience a loss of treatment benefit after Week 52 (defined as >20-point absolute worsening in total SALT score)... will be automatically retreated with their baricitinib dose, as randomized at Baseline."
